entries.instruction: Score whether the comment grounds any claim of implementation burden in concrete constraints. A 10 explains specific staffing, timing, equipment, workflow, or cost constraints and relates them to what implementation would require. A 0 asserts burden only as inconvenience, with no constraint described. Score the concreteness of the constraints described, not how heavy the burden is said to be.

entries.name: Identifies a specific analytical error in the agency's own analysis
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a specific defect in the agency's own analysis. A 10 points to a particular step, assumption, figure, or table in that analysis and explains concretely why it is wrong or incomplete. A 0 makes no reference to the agency's analysis at all. Score whether a specific analytical defect is identified, not how forcefully it is argued.

entries.name: Comparative tradeoff analysis
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment weighs plausible alternatives against one another. A 10 compares alternatives, states the advantages and disadvantages of each, and explains why the preferred option performs better. A 0 presents only a categorical conclusion with no alternative considered. Score the presence and completeness of the comparison, not which option the comment favors.

entries.name: Differentiated identification of affected stakeholder groups
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment distinguishes how the rule's impact differs across identified affected groups. A 10 names at least two distinct affected populations or entities and explains how the effect on them differs. A 0 refers only to a single undifferentiated group such as 'the public' or 'everyone', or does not identify who is affected at all. Score the differentiation actually stated in the text.

entries.name: Compliance feasibility grounded in how the work is done
entries.instruction: Score how concretely the comment shows what complying would actually require and uses that knowledge to evaluate the proposal. A 10 walks through the real sequence of work, access constraints, staffing, or timing and shows why the requirement is or is not achievable as written, ideally offering the achievable version. A 5 asserts that something is burdensome or unrealistic without describing the work; a 0 makes a demand with no account of how anyone would carry it out. Score detailed knowledge of the operation, not the force of the complaint.

entries.name: Substance survives deletion of the position statement
entries.instruction: Delete every sentence that states support, opposition, gratitude, feeling, or a purely procedural request, then score what remains. A 10 leaves a body of reasons, facts, or requested changes that stands on its own as regulatory input. A 5 leaves a thin residue: one reason, or a general consideration. A 0 leaves nothing, because the comment consisted entirely of a position, an attitude, an endorsement of someone else's filing, or a scheduling request.

entries.name: Monitoring and verification design
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment proposes a concrete way to tell whether the regulatory approach is functioning. A 10 specifies measurable monitoring, testing, reporting, feedback, or verification that would reveal how the approach is performing. A 0 asks for protection or compliance with no means of assessing it. Score the presence and specificity of the proposed check, not how important the underlying request seems.

entries.name: Detail-level concreteness of any proposed alternative
entries.instruction: Score how fully any alternative approach the comment proposes is specified in the text itself. A 10 lays out the mechanism -- steps, components, numbers, procedure -- in enough detail that another reader could implement or evaluate it. A 0 names an alternative without describing it, or points to a solution held outside the comment ('I already have one, contact me'). A comment proposing no alternative at all also scores 0.

entries.name: Causal mechanism linking action to stated goal
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment explains a specific causal chain connecting the proposed rule or action to the effect it claims will follow. A 10 traces an explicit mechanism ('X causes Y because Z') with enough specificity that a reader could evaluate whether the logic holds. A 0 states support, opposition, or a general value ('this is important', 'this is bad') with no explanation of how the action produces the claimed effect.

entries.name: States who would be affected and how, with concrete detail
entries.instruction: Score how concretely the comment states who would be affected and what would change for them. A 10 names the specific population, firms, or operations affected and describes in concrete terms what would be different for them under the rule. A 0 describes no affected party and no effect. Score the concreteness of the described effect, not how severe it is.

entries.name: Engages a named provision, alternative, or solicited question
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment both pinpoints something specific in the proposal -- a section, a defined alternative, a numeric threshold, a phrase, or a question the agency expressly asked -- and says what is wrong with it or answers it. A 10 does both, naming the exact target and giving the reason or answer, so the target is locatable without guesswork. A 5 pinpoints a target with only a bare preference attached, or reasons without landing on a locatable part. Pinpointing alone scores no higher than 4; a 0 addresses only the general subject matter of the rulemaking.

entries.name: Temporal and cumulative effects
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment's reasoning extends past immediate impacts to effects over time. A 10 analyzes delayed, repeated, cumulative, or long-term effects and says what unfolds over that horizon. A 0 confines its reasoning to a short-term assertion about immediate impact. Score the time horizon actually reasoned about in the text, not whether the analysis is correct.

entries.name: Quantified scale of real-world impact
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment supplies specific, position-relevant numbers establishing the scale of the problem or benefit the rule addresses. A 10 gives concrete, comment-specific figures -- dollar amounts, percentages, counts, timeframes -- that make the magnitude of the issue legible. A 0 gives no numbers at all, or only a generic or borrowed statistic not tied to the specific matter at hand. Score the specificity and relevance of the figures, not whether they favor any side.

entries.name: Concrete distributional effects
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies specifically affected or vulnerable groups and traces how they are exposed. A 10 names the group, describes its exposure or access pathway, and connects that pathway to a particular regulatory choice. A 0 refers only generically to the public, to fairness, or to unspecified harm. Score the concreteness of the group and the pathway described.

entries.name: Verifiable, attributable evidentiary sourcing
entries.instruction: Score the extent to which the comment's factual claims are attached to identifiable, checkable sources. A 10 gives specific citations to named studies, agency data, statutes, or official reports that actually support the claim made. A 0 states factual claims confidently with no source, or sources them to non-authoritative or unrelated material such as unnamed blogs, hearsay, or 'as I understand it'. Score the sourcing, not whether you agree with the claim.

entries.name: Supplies data the agency does not already have in the record
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment supplies information the agency would not otherwise possess. Score 10 when it provides measurements, operational records, survey results, or field observations and states where they come from. Score 0 when it supplies nothing beyond opinion. Judge whether new information enters the record, not whether it favors any position.

entries.name: Flags an ambiguous term and shows the interpretive consequence
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment isolates a specific word, phrase, or definition in the regulatory text and shows it admits two or more readings with different practical results. Score 10 when the term is quoted or cited to its section, the competing readings are laid out, and the divergent consequence of each is stated. Score 5 when it only calls a term unclear or asks for a definition without showing what turns on it. Score 0 when the operative text's wording is never engaged.

entries.name: Explains why the proposed approach will not achieve its stated aim
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment gives a reasoned account of a mechanism by which the rule as proposed would fail to produce the effect the agency states it intends. Score 10 when that failure mechanism is spelled out and reasoned through. Score 0 when no such account is given. Judge the reasoning offered, not the writer's confidence or tone.

entries.name: Monitoring, verification, and feedback design
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment proposes a way to check how the approach performs over time. Score 10 when it specifies measurable indicators, data collection, verification methods, reporting, or triggers for revisiting the approach. Score 0 when it offers no way to test or track performance at all.

entries.name: Distributional incidence and equity
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment differentiates who bears the costs and benefits. Score 10 when it names particular populations, firms, places, or users that face distinct costs or benefits and explains why exposure or access is unequal among them. Score 0 when effects are described only for an undifferentiated public.

entries.name: Generalized firsthand evidence
entries.instruction: Score whether firsthand experience is reported concretely and carried up to a general pattern. Score 10 when the writer gives specific observations from personal experience and translates them into a rule-relevant pattern that could hold beyond the writer's own case. Score 0 when the personal material is only anecdote, praise, or emotion, with no analyzable detail.

entries.name: Actionable procedural request with a reason tied to the record
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment requests a procedural step within the agency's power and gives a reason. Score 10 when a specific procedural action is requested — extend or reopen the comment period, defer action pending analysis, phase the effective date, re-notice, publish a tracking or timeline commitment — with a reason grounded in the record or the requester's circumstances. Score 5 when process is criticized but nothing is requested, or a request carries no reason. Score 0 when there is no procedural dimension.

entries.name: Legal authority and interpretive fit
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment connects the proposal to legal authority accurately. Score 10 when it ties the proposal to specific statutory language, delegated authority, precedent, or applicable legal limits, and states that connection correctly as far as the text shows. Score 0 when legal conclusions are asserted with no textual or doctrinal support.

entries.name: Rule-text pinpointing
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment targets identifiable rule text with a concrete revision. Score 10 when it names an exact proposed provision — by section, paragraph, or quoted language — and states a specific revision to that provision. Score 0 when the comment expresses only support or opposition with no identifiable rule-text target.

entries.name: Actionable amendment precision
entries.instruction: Score how precisely the comment specifies the change it asks for. Score 10 when it supplies exact replacement language, numeric thresholds, definitions, procedures, or parameters, stated concretely enough to be used as written. Score 0 when the requested action is only to do more, to act quickly, or a bare statement of support or opposition.

entries.name: Names a specific omission or missing commitment in the proposal
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies something the proposal fails to say, define, decide, or commit to, specifically enough for an agency to act on. Score 10 when it points to a particular gap — an unaddressed scenario, an undelivered commitment, an unassigned responsibility, an unanswered question the rule creates — and says what filling it would take. Score 5 when it calls the proposal incomplete without locating the gap. Score 0 when it engages only what the proposal does say.

entries.name: Evidence critique and uncertainty calibration
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment weighs the strength of the evidence it relies on. Score 10 when it distinguishes strong evidence from weak, names assumptions or limitations, and states confidence in proportion to the support offered. Score 0 when every claim is treated as certain or contrary evidence is passed over in silence.

entries.name: Feasible alternative design
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment offers an implementable alternative to the proposal. Score 10 when it proposes a concrete alternative, exception, threshold, or safeguard and explains how that variant still serves the proposal's stated legitimate objective. Score 0 when it offers only support, opposition, or an unelaborated demand. Score in between when an alternative is named but its fit to the objective is left unexplained.

entries.name: Explicit causal-mechanism / behavioral-response reasoning
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment traces a step-by-step causal chain from the rule to the effect it claims. Score 10 when each link in that chain is stated, including, where relevant, how affected parties would change their behavior in response. Score 0 when a harm or benefit is asserted with no account of the mechanism producing it. Score in between when a chain is offered but skips steps.

entries.name: Operational implementability
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment addresses what carrying the rule out would actually require. Score 10 when it identifies responsible actors, workflows, training needs, system dependencies, or failure modes that determine whether the rule can work in practice. Score 0 when implementation is treated as automatic, with no attention to who would do what or what could break.

entries.name: Ask serves more than the commenter's own burden or exposure
entries.instruction: Score who benefits from the change the comment requests, as the comment itself frames it. 10 = the change would improve the rule's functioning for third parties, the protected resource, or the public, including where it plainly costs the commenter something. 5 = the ask helps the commenter, but the stated reasons are about workability for everyone. 0 = the ask is entirely relief for the submitter (delay, exemption, a higher threshold, more time), and its public-interest framing adds no independent content.

entries.name: Implementation realism
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment addresses what carrying out the proposal would practically require. 10 = it maps specific steps, resources, timing, personnel, or supply-chain conditions needed to implement the proposal. 0 = it ignores implementation realities and treats the proposal as self-executing.

entries.name: Cross-rule and system interaction
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment relates the proposal to another rule, program, document, or process. 10 = it identifies a specific overlap, contradiction, gap, or sequencing problem with that other instrument and specifies how to resolve it. 0 = it analyzes the proposal in isolation and refers to no other rule, program, document, or process.

entries.name: Tradeoff and side-effect analysis
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment weighs the proposal's benefits against what it costs. 10 = it sets benefits against costs, risks, displaced protections, or unintended effects and states what the resulting tradeoff is. 0 = it presents one-sided approval or one-sided opposition, with nothing on the other side of the ledger.

entries.name: Quantified supporting evidence
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment supports its position with numbers. 10 = it uses relevant numerical data, calculations, comparisons, or rates that bear on its position and are stated concretely enough to be checked. 0 = it offers no verifiable quantitative support at all.

entries.name: Distributional consequence analysis
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies who bears distinct effects from the proposal. 10 = it names particular vulnerable, dependent, underserved, or differently situated groups and explains the mechanism by which those groups are affected differently. 0 = it invokes the broad public interest without identifying any affected group.

entries.name: Credible alternative meeting the regulatory objective
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment offers a worked alternative to the proposal. 10 = it proposes a specific alternative, exception, phase-in, or substitute and explains why that option can achieve the same regulatory objective, naming the relevant tradeoffs. 0 = it only registers support for or opposition to the proposal as written.

entries.name: Causal mechanism from provision to consequence
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment traces a causal chain from the proposed provision to a consequence. 10 = it follows the provision through specific behavior or implementation steps to a safety, health, environmental, or administrative consequence, with each link stated. 0 = it asserts that harm or benefit will occur without naming any intervening step.

entries.name: Applies a controlling standard to the facts rather than citing it
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment works the proposal's facts through a governing legal, scientific, or professional standard. 10 = the standard is named, its elements are identified, and the proposal's facts are matched against those elements to show fit or misfit, with that result driving the recommendation. 5 = a standard is invoked and a conclusion asserted, with the application left implicit. 0 = authority or the notice is quoted or summarized at length in place of analysis, or no standard is engaged.

entries.name: Audits the agency's own figures, record, or arithmetic
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment tests the agency's stated justification against numbers or statements the agency itself placed in the record. 10 = it reworks the agency's arithmetic, or sets the proposal against the agency's own admission or its own prior rule, and shows the figures so the check can be reproduced. 5 = it disputes a number but supplies no computation or source. 0 = the agency's figures are accepted or ignored, and the comment argues only from preference.

entries.name: Marks the limits of its evidence and reasons from them
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment separates what it knows from what it does not, and whether its recommendation follows from that separation. 10 = it states where the evidence runs out, names the specific unknowns, and gives a recommendation responsive to that uncertainty, such as precaution, a specified disclosure, or a question it says must be resolved first. 5 = uncertainty is acknowledged in passing and changes nothing. 0 = uniform certainty regardless of basis, or hedging with no consequence attached.

entries.name: Explicit evidence-to-requested-remedy linkage
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment draws an explicit, traceable line from the evidence or reasoning it presents to the exact provision, number, or action it asks be changed. 10 = the requested remedy is derived step by step from the stated evidence, so the derivation can be followed. 0 = evidence or complaint and a specific ask sit as disconnected pieces, with no traceable link between them.

entries.name: Surfaces an affected class or case the proposal overlooked
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a specific category of person, entity, or operating situation that the proposal's text does not appear to contemplate, or contemplates wrongly. 10 = a concrete class or edge case is named, its exclusion or misclassification is tied to specific proposal language, and the resulting harm or absurdity is stated. 5 = a gap is gestured at, but neither the class nor the consequence is made concrete. 0 = the comment discusses only the population the notice already addresses.

entries.name: Acknowledgment of tradeoffs and counterarguments
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment engages costs, competing interests, or plausible reasons for the opposite position. A 10 explicitly identifies and weighs a genuine tradeoff or counter-consideration while still holding its own position. A 5 mentions an opposing consideration but dismisses it without weighing it. A 0 is purely one-sided and shows no awareness that any opposing consideration exists.

entries.name: Challenge to agency assumptions
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment targets a specific premise, dataset, model, or inference in the proposal. A 10 identifies that particular element and presents concrete evidence or reasoning that could disprove or materially revise it. A 5 identifies the element but offers only assertion against it. A 0 merely disagrees with the proposal's conclusion.

entries.name: Reasoning-based persuasion vs rhetorical amplification
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment's persuasive force comes from developed reasoning and evidence rather than from rhetorical amplification. A 10 rests entirely on developed reasoning or evidence delivered in a measured tone, even when the position is strongly held. A 5 mixes real argument with heated rhetoric. A 0 substitutes capitalized or repeated demands, insults, or hyperbole for any developed argument.

entries.name: Identifies a conflict with operative statutory text
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment demonstrates a conflict between the proposal and controlling legal text. A 10 quotes or precisely cites the operative provision and shows the proposal cannot be squared with it, or that it triggers a procedure the statute requires and the notice omitted. A 5 cites a relevant statute or standard but asserts the tension rather than showing it. A 0 has no legal grounding, or cites authorities decoratively without showing any conflict.

entries.name: Names a specific omission in the agency's supporting analysis
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment locates a specific gap in the agency's own supporting analysis. A 10 points to a particular matter the notice, preamble, or impact analysis failed to address (an unexamined failure mode, an uncosted burden, an unanalyzed population, a required analysis not performed) and says why that omission bears on the decision. A 5 alleges inadequate analysis without locating the gap. A 0 never engages the agency's record.

entries.name: Ties a requested change to a specific paragraph of regulatory text
entries.instruction: Score whether a requested change is anchored to identified regulatory text. A 10 states what the comment wants changed and ties that request to a named paragraph, section, or table of the proposed text. A 5 requests a change and identifies only the broad part or topic it falls under. A 0 requests no change, or makes a request that names no provision. Score the anchoring, not the merit of the change requested.

entries.name: Tests whether the chosen instrument will actually bind
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment examines whether the proposed instrument would change behavior at all, not just its direction. A 10 asks or shows whether a numeric limit sits above observed practice, whether a threshold would ever be triggered, whether a voluntary approach has already been tried and failed, or whether the underlying model can resolve the regulated effect, and supports the answer. A 5 questions stringency without examining whether the instrument operates. A 0 argues only that the policy should be stronger or weaker.

entries.name: Traceable Evidence Use
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment's factual claims rest on support a reader could locate and check. A 10 identifies specific studies, datasets, statutes, official analyses, or clearly described observations, and explains their relevance and limitations. A 5 points to real sources but leaves their bearing or limits unstated. A 0 leaves claims unsupported or rests them on vague references such as 'studies show'.

entries.name: Unintended-consequence safeguards
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment pairs a plausible secondary harm with a concrete way to contain it. A 10 identifies a specific secondary failure or side effect and proposes a definite safeguard, monitoring step, exception, or contingency. A 5 identifies the secondary harm and its pathway but proposes no remedy. A 0 predicts harm without explaining the pathway or offering any mitigation.

entries.name: Viable alternative design
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment offers a practicable alternative regulatory design that still advances the proposal's stated objective while addressing the defect it identifies. A 10 describes such an alternative in enough detail that how it would work is clear. A 5 names an alternative direction without specifying any design. A 0 offers nothing beyond withdrawing the proposal or enforcing it as written.

entries.name: Distinguishes what the rule requires from what it merely permits
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment separates what the proposal would require from what it would merely allow. A 10 correctly identifies the mandatory and the discretionary elements and reasons about the difference between them. A 5 notes the distinction in passing without using it in any reasoning. A 0 treats the proposal as undifferentiated, drawing no line between mandates and options.

entries.name: Operational Feasibility
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment explains how affected parties would actually implement, administer, document, or comply with the proposed approach. A 10 walks through the concrete steps such compliance would take and names specific operational obstacles. A 5 raises implementation concerns only in general terms. A 0 treats implementation abstractly or not at all.

entries.name: Traceable causal chain from the rule to the claimed effect
entries.instruction: Score whether claimed consequences are connected to the rule by a mechanism a reader can follow and check. A 10 names the intermediate steps, making the claim falsifiable: the rule permits A, which changes B, which produces C. A 5 states one link and assumes the rest. A 0 asserts bare consequences with no pathway ('this will destroy the program'). Score the chain's presence and checkability, not agreement with its conclusion.

entries.name: Field observation that disconfirms a factual premise of the rule
entries.instruction: Score whether firsthand experience is aimed at a factual premise rather than at a preference. A 10 reports something the commenter directly observed, operated, or measured that contradicts a specific factual assumption the agency relies on (a stock estimate, an occupancy map, an achievability or exposure estimate), and names the assumption it contradicts. A 5 offers relevant firsthand experience as grounds for a preference, confronting no stated premise. A 0 reports no firsthand observation bearing on any premise.

entries.name: Specific, precise proposed regulatory fix
entries.instruction: Score how specifically the comment states the change it wants made to the proposal. A 10 supplies exact replacement wording, a specific numeric threshold, or an unambiguous procedural modification. A 5 names the direction of the change but leaves its substance unspecified. A 0 states only a general 'for' or 'against' position and offers no specific alternative.

entries.name: Identified accountable author with stated standing
entries.instruction: Score whether the text names the author or organisation and states a role, occupation, expertise, or regulated relationship to the rule's subject that lets a reader weigh its claims. Score 10 when both are present (for example, 'I have operated a licensed facility of this type for eleven years'). Score 5 when standing is asserted vaguely, naming no role, activity, or relationship. Score 0 when nothing establishes the writer's relation to the rule; salutations, signature blocks, titles, and letterhead never count.

entries.name: Reconciles conflicting evidence rather than citing one side
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment engages evidence pointing against its own position. Score 10 when it states what the contrary evidence is and explains how to reconcile it with the position the comment takes. Score 5 when contrary evidence is acknowledged but left unreconciled. Score 0 when only supporting evidence is presented. Judge the engagement with conflicting evidence, not which side of the question is right.

entries.name: Aggregated first-hand evidence from the represented population
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment reports what is actually observed across the population it speaks for and applies it to the rule. Score 10 for pooled or patterned evidence, such as survey results, recurring case types and how often they arise, ranges of practice across members, documented incidents, or variation between large and small participants, stated to imply a specific effect of the proposal. Score 5 for one or two concrete instances from its constituency, with no pattern established and no provision attached. Score 0 when breadth of members, customers, or dollars is claimed but nothing obser

entries.name: Provision-by-provision engagement with the proposed text
entries.instruction: Score how precisely the comment engages the content of particular proposed provisions. Score 10 when it identifies the specific provisions it addresses, states what each would require, and gives a reason directed at that requirement, so a reader can tell which parts it is about and what it says about each. Score 5 when it engages the proposal's substance only at the level of the rulemaking as a whole, without separating provisions. Score 0 when it expresses support, opposition, or general subject-area discussion without engaging what any particular provision would require; a docket or RIN cita

entries.name: First-hand operational and engineering particulars
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment supplies concrete technical or operational particulars drawn from hands-on work with the equipment, process, or facility the rule governs, tied to the requirement. Score 10 for specifics only such involvement yields: part or configuration numbers and what differs about them, observed failure or inspection findings and their frequency, actual labour hours or downtime, a conflict with an existing manual or procedure, an interval unmeetable for a stated physical reason. Score 5 when particulars are generic to the industry rather than the writer's own operation. Score 0 w

entries.name: Specifies how compliance would be demonstrated in practice
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment says concretely what a regulated party would have to record, measure, or show to demonstrate compliance, either under the proposal or under the comment's own alternative. Score 10 when the records, measurements, or showings are named specifically enough that a reader could carry them out. Score 5 when demonstration is mentioned only in general terms. Score 0 when how compliance would be demonstrated is not addressed. Judge the concreteness of the demonstration described, not whether it would be workable.

entries.name: Documented experience complying with the existing requirements
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment reports concrete experience of operating under the agency's current requirements and uses it to say how the proposal would work. Score 10 when it describes what compliance actually involved, such as steps performed, time or cost incurred, review timelines encountered, obstacles or workarounds, and connects that record to a specific effect of the proposed change. Score 5 when compliance experience is described but tied to no provision. Score 0 when nothing about what complying entailed is reported, or the proposal is discussed purely in the abstract; a relationship wit

entries.name: Numbers tied to a stated consequence for this rule
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment's figures are attached to an identified provision with a stated step from figure to conclusion. Score 10 when a figure's source is shown and the comment states what it implies for that provision ('the proposed 30-day window covers 4,200 filings at 6 staff-hours each, 25,200 hours the rule does not account for'). Score 5 when a sourced, relevant figure's inference to the rule stays implicit. Score 0 when no figure is linked by stated reasoning to a provision, however dense the statistics and cited reports.

entries.name: Substance carried over from the prior interaction
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment reports actual content from earlier dealings and applies it to this proposal. Score 10 when it states what was specifically learned, tested, agreed, required, or observed earlier and uses it as evidence about this rule ('the weekly sampling required by our 2022 authorisation produced no exceedances over 18 months, which bears on the frequency proposed here'). Score 5 when earlier work is described generally and only loosely tied to a provision. Score 0 when prior meetings, submissions, or collaboration are referenced but nothing from them is reported or brought to bea

entries.name: Specific legal defect identified with authority and cure
entries.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a legal defect specifically enough to be acted on. Score 10 when it names the particular statute, regulation, or procedural requirement, states what it requires, explains how the proposal departs from it, and states the change to the proposed text that would cure the departure. Score 5 when an authority is named and a conflict described but the mechanism or the cure is missing. Score 0 when unlawfulness or procedural defect is asserted without identifying which authority conflicts and how. Judge specificity only, not whether the legal argument is correct.
